Notebook introduction

This document provides an exhaustive, bit-by-bit technical breakdown of the **`Poly` (Polygon & Polyline) Subsystem** in the Retiam WebGPU Engine. It covers GPU compute stroke extrusion, non-zero & even-odd winding stencil fills, analytical rounded corner mathematics, raycasting, and zero-allocation dynamic vertex streaming.
1. Architectural Overview & Design Motivation

While [`Path`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Path.ts) is designed for complex SVG vector curves with cubic/quadratic béziers and analytical SDF raymarching, [`Poly`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Poly.ts) is Retiam's dedicated **high-performance linear geometry engine**:

blocks.text: 2. GPU Compute Stroke Extrusion Architecture ([PolyGeometry.ts](../src/engine/components/geometry/PolyGeometry.ts))

Instead of computing stroke offsets and miter joins on the CPU (which incurs heavy JS overhead and GC pressure for large polylines), `PolyGeometry` delegates stroke generation directly to **WebGPU Compute Shaders**:
A. Compute Dispatches in prepare():
B. The 4 Pass Configurations in PolyGeometry:

items: **`fill_stencil`**: Renders the GPU triangle mesh into the stencil buffer with either `Invert` (Even-Odd) or `Increment/Decrement` (Non-Zero) operations.
**`fill_cover`**: Renders the filled geometry testing the stencil buffer values.
**`stroke`**: Renders the extruded compute triangle strip with parameterized `uv` (for write-on animations) and local distance `d` (for sub-pixel anti-aliasing).
**`clear`**: Resets the stencil bitmask over the bounding quad.
